beats.say: A rider opens the app. The price must be fresh, now.
A batch job each hour is too slow. You need a stream.
beats.label: Why streaming
beats.head: Hourly is too slow

beats.say: Three ideas: the Kafka log, delivery guarantees, and event time.
beats.label: Track 10 · Streaming

check.prompt: Where does Kafka keep the order of messages?
check.why: Order holds inside a partition. Use the key to send related events to the same partition.

beats.say: First: Kafka is a log.
Producers append messages at the end. Consumers read at their own speed.
beats.label: The log
beats.head: Append at the end, read at your speed

beats.say: A topic is split into partitions. That is how Kafka scales.
beats.label: Partitions
beats.head: A topic has partitions

beats.say: Order holds only inside one partition. So the key decides what stays in order.
beats.label: Order
beats.head: Order is per partition

beats.say: Each consumer remembers its position. That position is the offset.
beats.label: Offset
beats.head: The offset is your position

check.prompt: A consumer processes a message, then crashes before it commits. What happens?
check.why: This is at-least-once delivery. So make the processing idempotent.

beats.say: Second: can a message be lost, or come twice?
At most once can lose a message. At least once can repeat one. Exactly once costs more.
beats.label: Three guarantees

beats.say: Most systems pick at least once, and make the write idempotent.
beats.label: In practice
beats.head: At least once + idempotent

beats.say: Third: events arrive late, and out of order.
A phone goes into a tunnel. Its events arrive ten minutes later.
beats.label: Example
beats.head: Ten minutes late

beats.say: So use the time the event happened. Not the time it arrived.
beats.label: Event time
beats.head: When it happened, not when it arrived

beats.say: A watermark says: I think I have seen everything up to this time.
beats.label: Watermark
beats.head: Seen everything up to here

beats.say: Last: a stream job remembers things.
A count per window is state. Flink saves that state in checkpoints.
beats.label: State
beats.head: State is saved in checkpoints

beats.say: After a crash, the job restarts from the last checkpoint.
beats.label: After a crash
beats.head: Restart from the checkpoint

beats.say: Quick recap of streaming.
Order is per partition. At least once, with idempotent writes. And use event time.
beats.label: Streaming

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
